name: Kenneth Tuchman
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, TTEC Holdings (Nasdaq: TTEC)
profile: California-born entrepreneur who founded TeleTech (now TTEC) in Los Angeles in 1982 and built it into a global customer-experience outsourcing firm; it moved to Denver in 1995 and IPO'd in 1996. He owns ~58% of TTEC; he proposed taking it private in 2024 but withdrew the bid in July 2025 citing market conditions.
interesting_fact: As a teenager he sold millions of puka shell necklaces to retailers, becoming one of the largest shell importers from the Philippines - where most of TTEC's international call centers are now located.
deep_cut_fact: TeleTech's breakthrough came after the 1984 AT&T breakup, when it was hired to monitor customer transitions - work that led to contracts with MCI and United Telecom (later Sprint). He and wife Debra co-founded the Tuchman Family Foundation in 1996, which runs 'Supplies For Success' school-supply drives.
notes: Take-private bid (2024) was withdrawn Aug 2025; TTEC remains public. Best route: TTEC media contact.

name: Boris Jordan
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Curaleaf Holdings (CEO since Aug 2024)
profile: Long Island-born son of Russian emigres who helped build Russia's post-Soviet capital markets in the 1990s (CSFB Moscow, co-founder of Renaissance Capital, Sputnik Group, ex-CEO of Gazprom Media). Back in the US, he invested in PalliaTech in 2014, which became Curaleaf, one of the largest US multi-state cannabis operators; he now runs it as chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: In 1995 Businessweek profiled him as 'the man who made Moscow's market' for his role in launching Russia's stock market and voucher privatization while co-heading CSFB's Moscow operation in his mid-20s.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his NYU bachelor's degree in the niche field of Russian-American Economic Relations, and worked closely with Bruce Gardner of the Russian Center for Privatization in the early 1990s.
notes: Forbes bio says 'executive chairman'; 2026 SEC filings list him as Chairman and CEO. Curaleaf proposed redomiciling to Delaware in 2026.

name: Wang Yu
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Guangzhou Ruoyuchen Technology (Ruoyuchen, SZSE: 003010)
profile: Born 1985, Wang Yu co-founded Ruoyuchen in Guangzhou in 2011 with his wife Wang Wenhui; it began as a Tmall/e-commerce operations agency and listed on Shenzhen in 2020 as China's 'first e-commerce agency stock'. It has pivoted to its own brands (laundry brand Zhanjia, supplements Feicui/Nuoyibei) and has pursued a Hong Kong (A+H) listing.
interesting_fact: After Ruoyuchen's share price surged in 2025, he told an interviewer the rally left him unable to sleep ('睡不着了'); the founding couple control about 43% of the company.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2021 interview he described entrepreneurship as 'a technical craft and a prolonged battle' (创业是一门技术活，更是一个持久战) and said 'the most important asset of a startup is people.'
notes: Common name; identity confirmed via Ruoyuchen. Best route is the company board-secretary/IR office.

name: Chen Mei-chi
current_role: Founder and Chairperson, Chenbro Micom (TWSE: 8210), also Chief Sustainability Officer
profile: Taiwanese entrepreneur (NCCU graduate, NTU MBA per data aggregators) who founded Chenbro in 1983 as one of Asia's first PC-chassis makers, then pivoted it from commoditised PC cases to server and cloud/AI-server chassis. Chenbro's 2025 revenue reached about NT$22 billion; she remains chair after the 2026 board re-election, with a professional CEO running operations.
interesting_fact: Her guiding motto since 1983 is '天道酬勤，商道酬誠' (heaven rewards diligence, business rewards integrity) - the company's Chinese name 勤誠 combines those two words. She brought in an outside general manager about 30 years after founding.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2026 she donated 100 lots (100,000 shares) of Chenbro stock to her alma mater National Chengchi University's 'Zhongni Fund' (仲尼基金), which rewards dedicated teachers rather than research output, alongside ex-TSMC executives Lora Ho and Li Ruei-hwa.
notes: Highly relevant to data-center theme (AI/cloud server chassis). No published IR email found; route via Chenbro corporate/IR page or MOPS spokesperson listing.

name: Hu Gang
current_role: Chairman, Newland Technology Group; controlling shareholder of Newland Digital Technology (SZSE: 000997)
profile: Fuzhou-born engineer (b. 1958, Fuzhou University automatic control) who founded Fujian Start Computer in 1988, then left in 1994 to found Newland Group. Newland Digital makes payment terminals/POS, barcode and IoT scanning hardware and runs merchant payment services; Hu controls it via Newland Group.
interesting_fact: Before founding Newland he founded Fujian Start (实达) Computer in 1988, aged 29, and later served as its group president; he left in January 1994 to start Newland.
deep_cut_fact: As a young engineer in 1989-90 he led development of the STAR-500 and STAR-600 Chinese/Western-language computer terminals, the latter a national Torch Program project; in 1992 he was promoted to senior engineer out of the normal sequence (破格).
notes: Bio details from user-contributed profile site (maigoo) consistent with company filings; Newland Digital chairman role may be held by others - Hu is group chairman/actual controller.

name: Han Jinghua
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Jiayou International Logistics (SSE: 603871); chairman of Guizhou Jialong Mining
profile: Chinese logistics entrepreneur who built Jiayou International from a Beijing freight forwarder into a listed cross-border logistics and infrastructure operator. With partner Meng Lian he controls about 43% of the company, which focuses on China-Mongolia coal corridors and Central African (DRC/Zambia) mining logistics and border-port infrastructure.
interesting_fact: Jiayou is building and operating the Zambian side of the Sakania dry port and the Ndola-Mufulira road, linking it to the Kasumbalesa-Sakania copper-belt crossing, and handled materials for the second China-Mongolia cross-border railway at Ganqimaodu.
notes: Very low public profile; little personal biography beyond filings. Company is relevant to energy/mining supply chains (coal, copper).

name: Wan Baifang
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Jiangsu ToLand Alloy (Tunan, SZSE ChiNext: 300855)
profile: Wan Baifang (万柏方, b. ~1968, Nanjing University EMBA) is the controlling shareholder of Jiangsu ToLand Alloy in Danyang, which makes cast and wrought superalloys and special stainless steels for aero-engines and gas turbines. He moved from running chemical plants into precision alloys around 2006, became chairman in 2015 and took the company public in 2020.
interesting_fact: ToLand's superalloy bars, wire, tubes and castings go into aero-engines and gas turbines ('两机') - the same turbine class used for on-site power generation - and it holds AS9100D aerospace quality certification.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1989 as a clerk in the equipment section of the Danyang Chemical Plant and ran chemical companies for over a decade before switching to precision alloys in 2006; he was also the company's chief engineer until January 2018.
notes: Chinese name is 万柏方 (Forbes romanisation 'Wan Baifang'). Co-controller with Wan Jinyi. Gas-turbine superalloy angle is relevant to data-center power.

name: Daniel J Starks
current_role: Independent Director, Abbott Laboratories (since 2017); former Chairman, President and CEO of St. Jude Medical
profile: Minnesota medtech executive who ran Daig Corp. (electrophysiology catheters) from 1986 until St. Jude Medical bought it in 1996, then rose to Chairman/CEO of St. Jude (2004-2015). He became executive chairman and, after Abbott's ~$25B acquisition of St. Jude in January 2017, joined Abbott's board, where he still serves (Form 4 filed April 2026).
interesting_fact: St. Jude Medical acquired his company Daig, a pioneer in catheters to diagnose and treat irregular heartbeats, in 1996 for roughly $425 million - the start of his two-decade path to running St. Jude.
deep_cut_fact: He was originally a lawyer brought in on Daig's long-running bankruptcy case; drawn to the company's heart-rhythm technology, he left his law practice to dig Daig out of bankruptcy and run it.
notes: Low public profile since 2017. Best route is via Abbott's board-communications process (Corporate Secretary) per Abbott proxy; not verified in this pass because search budget ran out.

name: Jun Rao
current_role: Co-founder, Confluent (now part of IBM after the acquisition closed March 17, 2026)
profile: Software engineer who co-created Apache Kafka at LinkedIn around 2008 with Jay Kreps and Neha Narkhede, then co-founded Confluent in 2014 to commercialise it. Confluent IPO'd in 2021; IBM agreed to buy it for about $11B in December 2025 and completed the deal in March 2026, making Kafka-based real-time data part of IBM's enterprise AI stack.
interesting_fact: Apache Kafka, which he co-created, became the de facto standard for streaming data; IBM framed the Confluent purchase as making real-time data 'the engine of enterprise AI and agents'.
deep_cut_fact: He is listed first on Apache Kafka's official committer roster (committer and PMC member), ahead of his co-founders - a nod to how hands-on he stayed with the codebase.

public_contacts.value: sarah.benchaita@ibm.com (IBM Software Communications, named on the Confluent acquisition release)

notes: Strong fit for data-infrastructure topic. Post-acquisition role at IBM not confirmed; Confluent site still lists him as co-founder. He writes on the Confluent blog (confluent.io/blog/author/jun-rao).

name: Joseph K Belanoff
current_role: Co-founder, CEO, President and Director, Corcept Therapeutics (Nasdaq: CORT)
profile: Psychiatrist (Amherst BA, Columbia MD) who co-founded Corcept with Stanford psychiatry chair Alan Schatzberg and has been CEO since its inception. Corcept develops cortisol modulators: Korlym (mifepristone) for Cushing's syndrome funded the pipeline, including relacorilant for Cushing's and platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.
interesting_fact: Corcept was born from Stanford psychiatry research on cortisol and psychotic depression; the company used revenue from Korlym to fund discovery of new selective cortisol modulators that, unlike mifepristone, do not terminate pregnancy.
deep_cut_fact: Even while running a public biotech, he has kept an academic post: he has held positions in Stanford's Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences since 1992 and is an Adjunct Professor of Psychiatry there.
notes: Biotech, not energy-related. Corcept's CHRO also heads communications (Amy Flood).

name: Qian Penghe
current_role: Chairman, General Manager and CEO, Quectel Wireless Solutions (SSE: 603236)
profile: Telecom engineer (b. ~1971) who founded Shanghai-based Quectel in 2010 and built it into one of the world's largest makers of cellular/IoT wireless modules (4G/5G, GNSS, Wi-Fi) used in meters, vehicles, payment terminals and industrial devices. He is the controlling shareholder (~15.6% direct) and runs the company as chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: Quectel's modules are embedded in a huge range of connected devices worldwide; it has expanded into ODM and antenna/one-stop IoT design services to serve global IoT customers end-to-end.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Quectel he worked his way through the handset industry as a hands-on engineer: test engineer at Hangzhou Motorola and Alcatel Shanghai Bell, project manager at UTStarcom and ZTE's Shanghai handset unit, then R&D VP at SIMCom.
notes: Bio from Quectel 2025 annual report (cninfo). Search budget exhausted, so no press interviews checked.

name: Zhang Yuping
current_role: Controlling shareholder (historically chairman) of Hengdeli Holdings (HKEX: 3389), formerly Xinyu Hengdeli; current title not verified
profile: Zhang Yuping's family bought the Hengdeli watch-retail business (a Beijing luxury-watch store dating to 1957) in 1997 and merged it with Shanghai Xinyu and Shanghai Watch Store into the Xinyu group in 2002. Xinyu Hengdeli listed in Hong Kong in 2005 and became China's largest luxury-watch retailer, with Swatch Group, LVMH and Temasek as strategic investors by 2007.
interesting_fact: By 2007, Swatch Group, LVMH and Temasek had all become strategic investors in his watch-retail group - a rare trio of backers for a Chinese retailer.
notes: Matched via Forbes 'Xinyu Hengdeli' = 新宇亨得利 (Hengdeli Holdings). Search budget was exhausted and the company site returned 403, so current role, alive status and contacts are unverified. Route: Hengdeli Holdings IR via HKEX filings.

name: Deni Bazhaev
current_role: Heir/shareholder of the Bazhaev family's Alliance Group interests (no confirmed executive title)
profile: Russian heir born in 1996, son of Alliance Group founder Ziya Bazhaev, who died in a March 2000 plane crash. As a minor he held about 29.9% of the holding controlling Alliance Oil (2007); the family sold its 60% oil-and-gas stake to Eduard Khudainatov's Independent Oil Company (NNK) in 2014. His wealth derives from those family holdings.
interesting_fact: Alliance Oil was founded through the Bazhaev family's Alliance Group; by 2007 the stake held in his name (29.9%) matched that of his uncle Musa Bazhaev, making him one of the largest shareholders while still a child.
notes: Very private; no public role, interviews or contacts found. Alive status inferred from his ongoing Forbes listing and Wikidata (no death date). Approach only via Bazhaev family/Alliance Group offices if at all. Search budget was exhausted.

name: Peng Wencheng
current_role: Chairman and President, BOMESC Offshore Engineering (SSE: 603727), Tianjin
profile: Offshore-engineering entrepreneur (b. ~1965) and actual controller of Tianjin-based BOMESC, which fabricates modules for LNG plants, FPSO topsides and FLNG for international energy majors and EPC contractors. He began at CNOOC's platform fabrication arm in 1987, ran Tianjin Bohai Oil Shipbuilding Engineering from 1996 and has chaired BOMESC since 2012.
interesting_fact: BOMESC has built process modules for some of the world's landmark LNG and oil projects, including Chevron's Wheatstone LNG, Russia's Yamal LNG and Petrobras' Mero 2 FPSO 'Sepetiba'.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1987 at CNOOC's offshore platform fabrication company (中海石油平台制造有限公司), rising to deputy head of the production-technology office and project manager before going independent in 1993.
notes: Strong energy (LNG/FPSO) fit. Bio from BOMESC 2025 annual report.
